questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The quality of the university and the experience of Iceland as a country to live in

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The incoming division from the host university was very good at providing the information needed

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There were held several events from the international division at the host university. Tutor meetings were also arranged and helpful to get information

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was not too difficult, but it was a bit far from the center and the campus

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It was cheaper than the student housing, but I would recommend student housing for sure! After two months I got an offer to live on campus, and I definitely preferred, even though it was more expensive.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was easy to choose courses and sign up for them, even though some courses required special documentation and were denied at first. Then I had to provide documentation for certain things related to either language skills or previous courses taken.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The incoming division was very helpful whenever needed

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: The timetable was not available until one week before semester start, and there were many overlaps - due to this I was forced to change some courses and couldn't get all the courses I wished to do

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure that you apply for a broad range of courses that you like. There will be overlap and you won't be able to follow all courses that you wish, so in this way you can choose better. Also make sure to get more courses pre-approved by the home university.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The quality of the courses was very good

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was overall very similar, however few things were different. There were more excursions in the course, which was very nice. Then, we had discussion sessions in smaller groups, were we had focus on different topics of the course, and had to present papers to our peers.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Soil Science
Natural hazards
Environmental Microbiology
Cartography and Map Design

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Definitely Soil Science and Natural hazards, as they are very specific for Iceland and very interesting! There are field trips in both of the courses, and they were amazing.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: When I moved in to the student housing, I had to buy my own router to get access to the internet.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: It was more or less the same level as Copenhagen, some things were cheaper, others were more expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The university has a gym on campus with really good prices for students. There is a bar on campus, which is the meeting point for all internationals, and has really good student prices as well.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Definitely Studentakjallarinn, the bar on campus. I took a language course, which was really interesting, but quite costly, but I would still recommend it.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Try to travel outside of Reykjavík as much as possible, there is so much to see and the weather usually is nicer outside of the capital :)

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It is not very easy to fully integrate in the Icelandic society. Mostly I was hanging out with other international students

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Sign up for the buddy exchange, it is a great way of getting to know local students and other internationals

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: It is hard to get to know Icelandic people at first, but when you really try, they are super nice! It is in this way kind of similar to Denmark

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I really enjoyed the abundance of outdoor activities and the spirit of it in the culture of Iceland

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Travel as much as you can
2. Apply for many courses, also pre-approval from KU
3. Enjoy the life outside of university

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Again, try to apply to many courses, so you have a backup in case they overlap and you have to change the course selection

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The experience of getting to know so many other international students in an easy way, the chance to get to know the culture and to see a lot of this beautiful country!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The weather (especially the constant strong wind) and the long nights in winter

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
